findings.evidence: "In addition, eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details the reviewer checks one at a time. The workspace must sit inside the employee's primary residence... [continues with nine more conditions presented as individual sentences]"
findings.fix: Convert this into a bulleted or numbered list where each workspace eligibility requirement is clearly separated.
findings.location: Eligibility section, paragraph beginning "In addition, eligibility for the workspace stipend..."
findings.violation: This paragraph strings together ten separate eligibility requirements as individual sentences within a single paragraph, making the list difficult to parse and remember.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Explicitly state what documentation is required when a photo of the receipt is insufficient.
findings.violation: This implies that a photo is insufficient for some requests but does not specify what documentation those cases require.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category."
findings.fix: Break into multiple shorter sentences that clearly explain when a second device per category is permitted and how it is tracked.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second paragraph
findings.violation: This is a single sentence with multiple nested clauses that is nearly impossible to parse and understand.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Restructure to reduce repetition, such as "You record it on the form. Finance then reconciles it against the request log each month, and Payroll releases the amount after that monthly review."
findings.violation: The phrase "stipend item" is repeated three times in three consecutive sentences.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Revise to use consistent pronouns throughout the document.
findings.violation: This section uses second-person pronouns ("you"), while the rest of the document uses "employees" or passive voice.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Either list all required steps here or clarify how this section relates to the more detailed "How to Apply" section.
findings.violation: This description omits the manager's approval form and purchase order mentioned in the "How to Apply" section as required.

findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Remove this duplicate sentence or replace it with information specific to special cases.
findings.violation: This sentence appears identically in the Program Overview section.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Remove duplicate sentences and clarify which entity is responsible for tracking the stipend budget.
findings.violation: The second sentence duplicates text from Program Overview. Additionally, this section attributes stipend budget tracking to the people operations office, contradicting Program Overview which attributes it to the benefits team.
